root_cause_label: Agent never read task specification, guessed extraction scope (all ALLOC sections) and used signed integers instead of unsigned, producing wrong output
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent spent 26 steps exploring the ELF binary without ever reading the task specification or expected output, then implemented extract.js with wrong section scope and signed-integer reads, and immediately claimed success without validating against any test harness.
t_err_evidence: Step 10 (think action): agent decides without consulting any task spec to extract '.rodata, .data, .got' sections as 4-byte integers keyed by decimal VMA addresses, adopting an unverified assumption about what the task requires.
t_commit_evidence: Step 27: agent writes extract.js that uses readInt32LE (signed) and extracts all SHF_ALLOC non-NOBITS sections (incorrectly including .text, .plt, .interp, .dynamic, etc.), locking in the wrong extraction scope and value type.
t_surface_evidence: Step 29 (cat out.json): output JSON contains many negative integers (e.g., -1073741822, -98693133) which are wrong output signals since ELF memory values in unsigned context should not be negative; output also covers far more addresses than expected.
trigger_explanation: The agent never looked for or read any task specification file, README, test script, or expected output. From the very start it relied on its generic ELF domain knowledge to guess what sections to extract and how to format values, without verifying against the actual task requirements. This led to wrong section scope (all ALLOC sections vs. just the key data sections), wrong value type (signed vs. unsigned 32-bit integers), and possibly wrong key format.
